first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence links onboarding simplification to improved time-to-value and activation. I would verify that evidence, while also checking the durability and revenue quality of promotional pricing given the competitor threat. A small guarded onboarding test is preferable to broad discounting because it directly addresses the current funnel deterioration while limiting the risk of admitting lower-quality accounts or weakening qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, since the verified source shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. This directly addresses the current declines in onboarding completion and activation and supports sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifts short-term qualified revenue by 18%, the 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal indicate poor long-term value. Measure activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and renewal/retention, while preserving uncertainty about whether the historical effect fully transfers to the current cohort.
